name: hh-meanrev-micro: vol-scaled deep fade, high-ATR regime only (5m)
rationale: MECHANISM: this variant isolates the CLAIM that the vol-scaled snapback is largest when volatility is elevated — it requires vol_realized to be ABOVE a fitted floor (a high-ATR regime) so the fade only fires where the dollar dislocation is big enough that a proportional reversion clears cost, and pairs it with an ATR-multiple stop so risk scales with the same regime. This is the deliberate mirror of the low-vol chop-gated fade: it bets that the deepest, most forced washouts (the ones that pay the fader most) live in HIGH vol, not low. Entry: bb_z deep washout AND rsi oversold AND vol_realized above a fitted floor; STOP = atr_mult x ATR. Long-only spot. DISCONFIRMER: this is a direct head-to-head with the low-vol chop-gated fade — if the high-vol regime does NOT show higher net-of-fee reversion, the snapback lives in calm ranges, not cascades, and this thesis is wrong — kill. Fatal cross-check: if the high-vol edge is entirely the top-5 liquidation days (exclude them and it vanishes), it is untradeable tail luck, not a repeatable high-vol snapback.
catalyst: deepest washout snapback in a high-realized-vol regime, ATR-scaled risk
